title: Lesson 10
paragraph: 会話・感情・対人関係

words.meaning: to avoid talking directly about the main subject
words.japaneseMeaning: 遠回しに話して本題を避ける
words.example: Please don't beat around the bush; tell me what went wrong.
meaningDistractors: hit the nail on the head

words.meaning: to persuade someone to do something
words.example: You should not talk someone into accepting a job they do not want.
words.usageNote: someone を相手に置き換え、into の後ろには名詞や -ing 形を置きます。

words.meaning: to persuade someone not to do something
words.japaneseMeaning: 説得して～を思いとどまらせる
words.example: It can be hard to talk someone out of making an impulsive purchase.

sentencePractice.prompt: When your aim is to persuade a person not to buy something, you try to ____ buying it.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Preventing the purchase by persuasion uses out of. Into encourages the purchase; helping with it assists rather than prevents it.

words.usageNote: someone を相手に置き換え、out of の後ろには名詞や -ing 形を置きます。

words.meaning: to remain angry with someone because of something they did in the past
words.japaneseMeaning: 過去のことを根に持つ
words.example: She apologized, and I do not want to hold a grudge.

words.meaning: to imagine another person's situation in order to understand their feelings
words.japaneseMeaning: 相手の立場に立って考える
words.example: Put yourself in your colleague's shoes before criticizing her decision.
Try not to lose your temper when the conversation becomes difficult.

words.meaning: to joke with someone by saying something that is not true
words.japaneseMeaning: 冗談を言って人をからかう
words.example: When he said he owned a castle, I knew he was pulling my leg.
meaningDistractors: give someone the benefit of the doubt

words.word: hit the nail on the head
words.meaning: to say exactly what is causing a problem or what is true
words.example: You hit the nail on the head when you said our instructions were unclear.

words.word: let the cat out of the bag
words.meaning: to reveal a secret, often by accident
words.japaneseMeaning: 秘密をうっかり漏らす
words.example: Don't let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.

sentencePractice.prompt: The party was meant to be a secret, but I accidentally mentioned it in front of the guest of honor. I did not mean to ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Accidentally disclosing the secret lets the cat out of the bag. Both other phrases describe keeping information concealed or uncertain.

words.meaning: to stop yourself from saying something you would like to say
words.japaneseMeaning: 言いたいことをぐっとこらえる
words.example: Sometimes you need to bite your tongue and let the other person finish.
meaningDistractors: let the cat out of the bag
